decisions.question: vision.md conflicts on who gets a dashboard at launch: section 15 says Admin only, while sections 13, 32 and 37 include business-owner login. Which scope should the first release use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Only Admin creates businesses and edits pages. Business-owner login is deferred, following section 15 of vision.md.

decisions.question: Which language should the five documents use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Write all five documents in English with consistent terminology. Interview questions can remain in Arabic.

decisions.question: vision.md treats analytics as optional. What analytics belong in the first release?
decisions.selectedDescription: No product scan counters or visit history in the first release. Operational error monitoring remains separate.

decisions.question: Should the first release include the optional /b/{slug} business sharing link alongside /c/{Card ID} card links?
decisions.selectedDescription: Provide a business sharing link separate from card links. Changing the slug does not change printed QR codes or NFC destinations.

decisions.question: Section 28 proposes, but does not commit to, Next.js with Supabase PostgreSQL, Auth and Storage. Should we adopt this stack?
decisions.selectedDescription: One Next.js application with internal modules, using managed Supabase PostgreSQL, Auth and Storage. Less operational work, but identity, data and images depend on one provider.

decisions.question: Which managed application-hosting direction should the launch architecture use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Prefer application hosting on Cloudflare. Framework, runtime and caching compatibility must be checked before implementation.

decisions.question: vision.md specifies a public card token but not database primary-key types. Which internal identifier policy should we adopt?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use internal UUIDs for cards, businesses and content, separate from printed card tokens. If Supabase Auth is adopted, reuse its user identity. UUIDs are larger than bigint but support imports across environments.

decisions.question: How should card-inventory imports handle invalid rows and cards that already exist?
decisions.selectedDescription: Preview before importing. Invalid rows or duplicate tokens within the file reject the batch. Existing tokens are skipped unchanged; new cards are Inactive and unlinked. Requests to import Active cards are rejected.

decisions.question: An Active card belongs to Alfa Cafe and needs to move to Beta. Which card-transfer lifecycle should the first release support?
decisions.answer: 1 , store the history from day one with simple ui

referencedOption.label: Deactivate first (Recommended)
referencedOption.description: Admin deactivates the card, reassigns it while Inactive, then activates it separately. Deactivation preserves assignment; unassigning clears it and deactivates. No card deletion or token reuse in v1.

decisions.parentInterpretation: Option 1 plus mandatory operational Card history from day one with simple UI; separate from deferred analytics.

decisions.question: When should a business page become public, and what should disabling the business do?
decisions.selectedDescription: Create businesses Disabled. Admin enables the page when ready; subsequent saves publish immediately. Disable blocks all card links, business links and aliases without changing card assignments/status. No business hard deletion in v1.

decisions.question: With business-owner login deferred, should the first-release business model omit owner-account links or retain a dormant optional link?
decisions.selectedDescription: Do not store an owner-account link on businesses in v1. Admin operates the product but is not the business owner. Decide future ownership migration separately.

decisions.question: After /b/alfa-cafe changes to /b/alfa, what should happen to the old business link?
decisions.selectedDescription: Keep old slugs as aliases redirecting to the same business; never assign them to another business. Disabling the business blocks its aliases too.

decisions.question: Should each built-in section type appear only once on a business page, or can Admin add multiple sections of the same type?
decisions.selectedDescription: Hero, Contact, Social, Payments, Location, Hours, Reviews and Custom Links each appear at most once. Admin can show, hide and reorder them; this is not a page builder.

decisions.question: How should Admin enter business opening hours in the first release?
decisions.selectedDescription: Store seven days with closed flags or multiple opening/closing intervals and a business timezone. No holiday calendar or calculated open-now status in v1.

decisions.question: vision.md includes both contact fields and typed WhatsApp links. Which source of truth should contact buttons use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Phone, WhatsApp and email fields are the authoritative contact data. Contact buttons derive from them; generic links cannot create competing contact buttons.

decisions.question: Should payment items only open external links, or also display payment identifiers that visitors can copy?
decisions.selectedDescription: Each payment item opens a valid external URL. NexTap does not process or verify payments and does not display wallet numbers for copying.

decisions.question: For Next.js application hosting on Cloudflare, should we select a runtime adapter now or target Workers and defer the adapter until compatibility checks?
decisions.selectedDescription: Commit to Cloudflare Workers for the full-stack app, but select vinext or OpenNext only after testing project compatibility. Keep that test as a pre-implementation requirement.

decisions.question: What environment separation should the launch architecture require?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use separate staging and production Workers and Supabase services, preventing staging writes from touching production data or authentication.

decisions.question: With Supabase PostgreSQL selected, which schema-migration policy should the database specification adopt?
decisions.selectedDescription: Keep reviewed SQL migrations in the repository, test them before production and prohibit undocumented dashboard-only production schema edits. Environment promotion and restore gates remain architecture decisions.

decisions.question: When a card and its business are eligible for public display, should /c/{Card ID} render the page directly or redirect to /b/{slug}?
decisions.selectedDescription: Serve the business page directly at /c/{Card ID}, without redirecting. The card URL remains independent of the business slug.

decisions.question: Should Admin operations use a documented private HTTP/JSON API at /api/admin, or internal Next.js Server Actions?
decisions.selectedDescription: Document a private /api/admin HTTP/JSON contract, not a public SDK. Use internal UUIDs for Admin resources, explicit commands for card actions and defined read/update/reorder methods.

decisions.question: Which error-response format should Admin operations use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use {error:{code,message,fieldErrors?,requestId}}. Codes are stable, messages disclose no secrets or stack traces and the UI handles translation.

decisions.question: Should card inventory upload accept CSV only, or also accept XLSX directly?
decisions.selectedDescription: Accept UTF-8 CSV exported from Excel, with card_id and optional status that must be Inactive. Preserve existing printed tokens. Security will define size and row limits.

decisions.question: Q24: What authentication should Admin accounts use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Individual accounts, no public signup, Supabase email/password plus mandatory authenticator-app TOTP MFA for privileged access.

decisions.question: Q25: What randomness standard should newly generated public card IDs meet?
decisions.selectedDescription: Future IDs use at least 128 cryptographically random bits. Preserve existing printed IDs exactly. Public IDs grant no permissions.

decisions.question: Q26: What image-upload limits and sanitization should the first release require?
decisions.selectedDescription: JPEG/PNG/WebP only, maximum 2 MiB and 16 megapixels; decode/re-encode, strip metadata, reject SVG and animation.

decisions.question: Q27: How long should routine Admin audit metadata, operational errors and temporary import/upload data be retained?
decisions.selectedDescription: Admin audit metadata 90 days, operational errors 14 days, unused import/temp uploads 24 hours. Card history is separate.

decisions.question: Q28: For day-one card history and its simple UI, which events should be visible? Retention will be a separate question.
decisions.selectedDescription: Record creation/import, Assign/reassign, Activate, Deactivate and Unassign when state or assignment actually changes. Include Admin, time, old/new business and status. Simple read-only per-card Admin timeline; no scans or content snapshots. Rejections stay in security audit.

decisions.question: Q29: What minimum content must a business have before Admin can enable its public page?
decisions.selectedDescription: Require a nonempty business name and unique slug. Contact, links, hours, location and both images are optional; Admin can enable a minimal page.

decisions.question: Q30: How should generic links belong to sections, and can a business have multiple links for the same platform?
decisions.selectedDescription: Each generic link belongs to exactly one supported link-bearing section and appears once. Multiple links to the same platform are allowed with distinct labels. Contact buttons still come from contact fields.

decisions.question: Two Admin tabs read the same card or business. After one saves, should the stale tab be rejected or allowed to overwrite the newer value?
decisions.selectedDescription: Require the version originally read by the editor and reject stale writes without changes. Successful card mutations and their history commit atomically.

decisions.question: May Admin activate an assigned card while its business is still Disabled?
decisions.selectedDescription: An assigned card can become Active while its business is Disabled, but public requests still cannot show that business until Enabled. Supports preparing inventory before launch.

decisions.question: After card deactivation/reassignment or business Disable, must every new request check current eligibility, or is up to 60 seconds of stale access acceptable?
decisions.selectedDescription: Check current assignment/status and business eligibility for each new card/business/alias request before serving cached content. Unknown eligibility returns unavailable. Already delivered or in-flight copies cannot be recalled.

decisions.question: After business Disable or logo/cover replacement, should old direct image URLs stop serving the image, or may sanitized artwork remain public?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use private storage and application-mediated delivery checking Enabled business and current image reference. Disable or replacement stops new access through old URLs. Previously downloaded/browser-cached copies cannot be recalled.

decisions.question: How long should the successful card-lifecycle history be retained?
decisions.selectedDescription: Keep minimal append-only operational history for the permanent card's lifetime. Store actor UUID, time, old/new business and status, not IPs, content or copied actor emails. Admin-only timeline; separate from 90-day audit expiry.

decisions.question: Which Admin session limits, sensitive-action reauthentication and recovery policy should the first release require?
decisions.selectedDescription: Server-enforced 8-hour absolute and 30-minute idle expiry; TOTP within 5 minutes for reassignment, enabling businesses, payment-link or Admin-permission changes. Trusted operator handles bootstrap/MFA recovery with out-of-band verification and audit. Validate current membership each privileged request; verify enforcement feasibility.

decisions.question: Which authorization and database-access pattern should Admin operations and public reads use?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use current verified Admin membership and MFA, identity-scoped management clients, RLS/limited grants and same-business child constraints. Deny anonymous management-table access; public reads use a restricted projection. Server-only privileged keys require explicit scope checks. Protect cookie mutations against CSRF.

decisions.question: Should the documents adopt these content-safety rules and numerical limits for the first release?
decisions.selectedDescription: Plain text, HTTPS web links without credentials, validated derived contact links; no scripts/HTML/arbitrary server URL fetches. Limits: name 120, description 1000, label 80, URL 2048 characters; 50 links/business; 8 KiB settings/section. Validate registered section/icon schemas before persistence.

decisions.question: Which first-release throttles and CSV import limits should protect authentication and Admin operations while keeping public pages broadly reachable?
decisions.selectedDescription: Login/recovery 10 attempts/15 min; MFA 5/10 min, using account and trusted-IP controls. Per Admin: mutations 120/10 min, uploads 20/10 min, imports 5/hour. CSV cap 10,000 rows/10 MiB; preview expires after 30 min. Stable 429 errors/retry guidance; public routes use volumetric protection without a low blanket visitor quota.

decisions.question: If an Admin data change cannot save its required audit record, should the whole change fail or may routine audit logging be best effort?
decisions.selectedDescription: Commit minimized Admin audit metadata with each successful administrative data mutation; required card history stays in the same transaction. If audit storage fails, reject the mutation. Failures after database commit, such as cache or image-delivery failures, cannot pretend the data rolled back.

decisions.question: Should application logs minimize visitor data, with a required prelaunch review of provider-native logs and backups, or retain additional incident metadata?
decisions.selectedDescription: Application errors record requestId, route template and redacted errors, not visitor IPs/identifiers, full public tokens, queries, bodies or secrets. No visitor tracking. Restrict operator access and verify provider-native log/backup retention and deletion behavior before launch rather than assuming application periods apply.

decisions.question: How should the Admin API express lifecycle commands and content edits?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use explicit POST commands for Assign/Unassign/Activate/Deactivate, PATCH for business fields and PUT for complete section/link order lists. Enforce the approved lifecycle rules.

decisions.question: How should the Admin API handle retrying commands after a timeout?
decisions.selectedDescription: Require Idempotency-Key for effectful commands and expectedVersion for edits. Repeating a key with the same payload returns the original result; a different payload is rejected. Key-retention duration still needs a defined contract.

decisions.question: Which HTTP status mapping should the documented API adopt? This does not decide whether all public lifecycle notices look identical.
decisions.selectedDescription: 401 missing session, 403 forbidden, 404 missing/non-disclosed resource, 409 version/lifecycle conflict, 422 semantic field validation, 429 rate limit, 503 unavailable dependency. Admin errors use the approved JSON envelope. Preserve the required safe Inactive-card notice without exposing assignment/history/Admin data.

decisions.question: How should Admin card and business list endpoints paginate results?
decisions.selectedDescription: Use opaque cursors, bounded limits and stable sorting. Return nextCursor without exposing sensitive internal data.

decisions.question: Should numerical operating targets be chosen now, or remain explicit mandatory prelaunch gates?
decisions.selectedDescription: Do not invent budget, SLA, latency, region, recovery-time or acceptable-data-loss targets. Keep them as mandatory prelaunch decisions verified against provider plans.

decisions.question: With fresh fail-closed eligibility checks already required, how should public requests avoid showing old business content after a save?
decisions.selectedDescription: Save content and increment its revision atomically. Each request reads fresh eligibility and revision, then uses cached public content keyed by business+revision. On a miss load current content; a cache-write failure does not fail a valid read. Publication does not depend on successful global purge.
